---

## State of the work

### What the job is
Issue **#364** (sub-issue of **#149**, "PR-by-number 読みの共有リーダーへの統合と、残す箇所の理由記述"), a follow-up to **#345**'s 直し方 2・3:

1. Move the pr-by-number reads in `src/` onto one shared reader, expressing projection differences (e.g. `{title, headRefName}` vs. the whole object) as arguments; model is #343's `thread.ts` + `tests/contract/comment-read-sites.test.ts` (a set closed in both directions).
2. Where a read stays independent, write **why** beside the code.
3. Judge each site's "why it was independent" before folding it in.

**#345's three acceptance criteria were already met by PR #363** (review-comment paging, `merge-signals` retry-policy unification, existing tests green) — those two fixes were not redone.

Acceptance criteria for #364: reads folded into the shared reader; each remaining independent read explains itself in code; existing PR-read tests pass (incl. #363's paging/retry tests); the contract test set is closed in both directions (if added). Close condition: verified in code on the **head of a PR merged into `atomaton/issue-149`**.

### What is done (PR #368 — MERGED into `atomaton/issue-149`)
New **`src/adapters/github/pull-request.ts`** — the one reader:
- `PullRequestFields = string | readonly string[]`; `PullRequestRead<T> = {known:true,value} | {known:false,why}`; `PullRequestDiffRead`.
- `viewArgs()` (the single `pr view` argv, `:80`), `whyNot()` (names the read), `readPullRequest()`, `readPullRequestOrThrow()`, `readPullRequestObject()` (`gh api repos/<repo>/pulls/<n>`), `readPullRequestDiff()` (`Accept: application/vnd.github.v3.diff`).
- Every read uses retrying `ghRead`. **Failure policy stays with each caller** (`known`/`why` rather than throwing, except the explicit OrThrow).

Call sites moved (all verified by grep — no `pr view` / `pulls/${…}` left outside the reader and the three exempt files):
- `merge-signals.ts` (`:239`-equivalent + `mergeStateStatus`; local `tryJson` deleted, `mergeStateStatus` dropped from `PullRequestView`), failure → `throwOnFailure` / degrade to `UNKNOWN`.
- `workspace-scope.ts` (`body`) — logs, falls back to a private workspace.
- `lib/pr-head-branch.ts` — `prHead()` now takes parsed `PrHeadView | null | undefined` instead of a JSON string; `PR_HEAD_FIELDS` const is module-private.
- `mcp/github.ts` — `:1398`, `:1561`, `:1679`, `:1849` → `readPullRequestOrThrow`; `:1570` → `readPullRequestDiff`.
- `fetch_events.ts` — REST object → `readPullRequestObject`; diff → `readPullRequestDiff`.
- `validate_pull_request.ts` — head/base → `readPullRequest(…, ["headRefOid","baseRefName"])`; body → `readPullRequest(…,"body")` (degraded, not fatal).

Left independent, each with a reason in code **and** in the contract test's `NOT_A_READ`:
- `merge-signals.ts` — `pulls/<n>/files?per_page=100` (paginated, fails **closed**).
- `fetch_events.ts` — `pulls/<n>/reviews`, `pulls/<n>/comments` (review lists for model context, degrade to empty).
- `mcp/github.ts` — `pulls/<n>/comments?per_page=100` (#363's paged reviewer read, untouched).

New tests: `src/adapters/github/pull-request.test.ts` (5) and `tests/contract/pr-read-sites.test.ts` (3, closed both ways). Test fixtures updated in `resolve_pr_branch.test.ts` (now asserts the `unreadable` refusal + "the answer was not JSON") and `validate_pull_request.test.ts` (two `pr view` rules instead of one REST rule).

Behaviour changes made deliberately, already reported in the PR — **do not revert**:
1. `pr-head-branch.ts` and `workspace-scope.ts` now retry a transient read.
2. Unparsable JSON is a failed read (`unreadable`), not `no-branch`; empty stdout is a failed read.

Validation actually run: `bun run typecheck` clean; `bun run test` **2086 pass / 0 fail / 168 files**; `bun run lint` (tsc + synth) clean; `dist/` is gitignored, nothing generated committed.

### Review outcome
Reviewer found **no merge-blocking defect**; the merge gate fired only on `src/adapters/github/merge-signals.ts` (governed path), leaving the merge to a person — it has since been merged. One non-blocking coverage note worth passing on: the `NOT_A_READ` exemptions are per **file**, so a `gh pr view` for the pull request itself reintroduced inside `mcp/github.ts` would pass the contract test. The set of *files* is still closed both ways, which is what #364 asked for.

### What is still open
Only the post-merge judgement and the closing call. This run is on `main` (`6bcdc62`, self-deploy v0.21.44); **raw `git fetch` is blocked by the shell guard**, so the merged head of `atomaton/issue-149` must be read with the `fetch` tool (`raw.githubusercontent.com/.../atomaton/issue-149/<path>`) or judged from the merged diff already in the thread.

Assessment to act on: all four acceptance criteria are met (shared reader; reasons beside every remaining read; full suite green including #363's; contract set closed), and the close condition — merged into `atomaton/issue-149` — is satisfied by #368.

### What must not be redone / must not be forgotten
- Do **not** re-do #363's paging or the `merge-signals` retry policy.
- Do **not** make further code changes to what merged.
- Do not re-open or re-create a PR; #368 is merged.
- Ending: call `request_close_issue` with the report in its `summary` argument (the call ends the session, so the report must be written in the call's own text — conclusion, how you know with `path:line` anchors, what you could not establish, what happens next). A message with two calls is refused.

Atomaton: the pull request for this issue merged. Decide whether what merged satisfies what this issue asked for. Say which acceptance criteria are met and which are not; conclude the issue when they are met, and carry on with the work when they are not.

The people you may call in your closing message: @yuma-seno. @yuma-seno is the one this work belongs to.

A closing message calls at most one thing: one agent, as a line holding nothing but `/name`; or one of those people, as a single `@login`; or nobody, and the machinery tells the person this work belongs to. A mention of one of them is a call — write one only when you are handing the work to them. Two calls, an agent and a person or two of either, are refused: the message is posted with its mentions left as text, nothing in it is started, and the machinery makes the call itself.

{"baseRefName":"atomaton/issue-149","createdAt":"2026-10-25T08:52:53Z","headRefName":"atomaton/issue-364","number":368,"state":"MERGED","title":"Read a pull request by number in one place (#364)","body":"/reviewer

Part of #364
## What changed

`src/adapters/github/pull-request.ts` is now the only place in `src/` that spells a
pull request's own endpoint. It owns the argv, the retry (`ghRead`, not `gh`) and the
name a failure carries; the **projection is an argument**, because `{title,
headRefName}` and the whole object are different questions of one object.

Three functions, because three questions:

| function | read | answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `readPullRequest(repo, n, fields)` | `gh pr view <n> --json <fields>` | `{known, value}` / `{known:false, why}` |
| `readPullRequestOrThrow(...)` | the same | the value, or an exception naming the read |
| `readPullRequestObject(repo, n)` | `gh api repos/<repo>/pulls/<n>` | the whole REST object — the one projection `--json` cannot express |
| `readPullRequestDiff(repo, n)` | the same endpoint, `Accept: …v3.diff` | the patch |

What a failure **means** stays with each caller, as `comment-read-sites.test.ts` states
for the comment reader: `merge-signals.ts` throws through its injected
`throwOnFailure`, `pr-head-branch.ts` returns an `unreadable` refusal that quotes the
reason, `workspace-scope.ts` logs and falls back to a private workspace,
`validate_pull_request.ts` stops before writing checks, `mcp/github.ts` fails the tool.

## The thirteen sites, and what happened to each

<details><summary>per-site decision</summary>

| site | was | now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace-scope.ts:20` | `pr view --json body --jq .body` | `readPullRequest(…, "body")`; a failed read logs and gives a private workspace |
| `merge-signals.ts:239` | `pr view --json isDraft,author,…` | `readPullRequest` with the same eight fields; failure → `throwOnFailure` |
| `merge-signals.ts:266` | `pr view --json mergeStateStatus` | `readPullRequest`; failure degrades to `UNKNOWN`, which already blocks |
| `lib/pr-head-branch.ts:92` | `pr view --json headRefName,isCrossRepository` | `readPullRequest`; the tolerant `prHead` now takes the parsed answer |
| `mcp/github.ts:1398`, `:1561`, `:1679`, `:1849` | four `pr view` calls | `readPullRequestOrThrow` with each list |
| `mcp/github.ts:1570` | `gh pr diff` | `readPullRequestDiff` |
| `fetch_events.ts:259` | REST object | `readPullRequestObject` |
| `fetch_events.ts:278` | `gh api … -H Accept: …diff` | `readPullRequestDiff` |
| `validate_pull_request.ts:461` | REST object, `head.sha` / `base.ref` | `readPullRequest(…, ["headRefOid","baseRefName"])` |
| `validate_pull_request.ts:537` | REST object, `--jq .body` | `readPullRequest(…, "body")`, still degraded rather than fatal |

</details>

## What stays independent, and why it is written down

A sub-resource is not a field of the pull request. Each of these now says so beside the
code, and `tests/contract/pr-read-sites.test.ts` lists them with the reason:

- `merge-signals.ts` — `pulls/<n>/files?per_page=100`: a paginated list that fails
  **closed** (an unreadable list must block a merge), where every projection of the
  request itself degrades.
- `fetch_events.ts` — `pulls/<n>/reviews` and `pulls/<n>/comments`: lists of review
  objects for the model's context, which degrade to empty rather than throwing.
- `mcp/github.ts` — `pulls/<n>/comments?per_page=100`: the same list projected for a
  reviewer (#363's paged read, unchanged).

## Verification

Ran here, on the branch:

- `bun run test` — **2086 pass, 0 fail** (168 files), including #363's paging and retry
  tests (`merge-signals.test.ts`, `list_pr_review_comments reads every page`) and the
  new `pull-request.test.ts` (5 tests: projection-is-the-argument, retry, refusal names
  the read, unparsable answer, object+diff endpoints) and
  `tests/contract/pr-read-sites.test.ts` (3 tests, closed in both directions).
- `bun run lint` (`tsc --noEmit` + `synth`) — clean; `dist/` is gitignored, nothing
  generated is committed.

Two behaviours changed deliberately, both in the direction #345 argued:

1. `pr-head-branch.ts` and `workspace-scope.ts` now **retry** a transient read. The
   `resolve_pr_branch.ts` test that pinned "output that is not the JSON asked for is no
   branch either" now sees the `unreadable` refusal with "the answer was not JSON"
   instead of `no-branch` — same outcome (no branch, exit 0), a more accurate sentence.
2. A pull request answered with **empty stdout** by `gh pr view` is now a failed read
   rather than an empty object. `gh` does not do this on success; it stops an empty
   answer being read as a pull request with no fields.

## Base

Stacked on `atomaton/issue-149`, as a sub-issue of #149 requires. No further work is
needed for #345's other two acceptance criteria — #363 delivered the paging and the
merge-signals retry policy, and both are untouched here apart from sharing the new
reader.

---
_Opened by [`engineer`](https://github.com/yuma-seno/atomaton/actions/runs/40177381793)_

{"reason": "PR #368 が atomaton/issue-149 にマージされ、#364 の受け入れ条件4点とクローズ条件（親ブランチにマージされた PR のヘッドでコード確認できること）がすべて満たされた。", "summary": "## 結論: #364 の受け入れ条件は4点すべて充足、クローズ条件も満たしています

マージ済み PR: **#368**（base `atomaton/issue-149` / `state: MERGED`）。確認は親ブランチのヘッド **`atomaton/issue-149` = `8d85e67`** 上のコードで行いました（この run の作業ツリーは `main` `6bcdc62` のままで、シェルの fetch は塞がれているため、`raw.githubusercontent.com/.../atomaton/issue-149/<path>` で実ファイルを読み出して確認しています）。

### 受け入れ条件ごとの判定

1. **PR-by-number の読みが共有リーダーに統合されている（射影は引数）— 充足。**
   `src/adapters/github/pull-request.ts` が唯一の読み手です。射影は `PullRequestFields`（`string | readonly string[]`）として引数化され、argv の組み立ては `viewArgs()` の一箇所だけ（`["pr", "view", …]` の出現はファイル内で1回、契約テストがそれを固定）。答えは `PullRequestRead<T>` = `{known:true,value}` / `{known:false,why}`。失敗の意味づけは呼び出し側に残し、例外が欲しい呼び出しだけ `readPullRequestOrThrow` を使う形です。全読みが `ghRead`（再試行あり）を通ります。
   13箇所の移設は PR 本文のサイト別表のとおり: `merge-signals.ts`（8フィールド射影＋`mergeStateStatus`）、`workspace-scope.ts`（`body`）、`lib/pr-head-branch.ts`（`headRefName,isCrossRepository`）、`entrypoints/tools/mcp/github.ts` の4つの `pr view` と `gh pr diff`、`fetch_events.ts` の REST オブジェクトと diff、`validate_pull_request.ts` の head/base と body。
   マージ後のヘッドで直接確認したもの: `src/adapters/github/merge-signals.ts` は `import { readPullRequest } from "./pull-request.ts"` を持ち、`PullRequestView` から `mergeStateStatus` が消えています。

2. **独立のまま残した読みに、コードのそばで理由が書かれている — 充足。**
   `merge-signals.ts` の `readChangedFiles()` には「Not `pull-request.ts`'s read, and the reason is the question: …paginated sub-resource (`pulls/<n>/files`)… this one fails CLOSED, where every projection of the request itself degrades」と、サブリソースであること・fail-closed であること・fail-closed にする理由までが書かれています。同じ理由づけが `fetch_events.ts`（`pulls/<n>/reviews`, `pulls/<n>/comments` → 空に縮退）と `mcp/github.ts`（`pulls/<n>/comments?per_page=100`、#363 のページ読みそのまま）にも置かれています。理由はモジュール冒頭の「What this module does not read」節にも要約されています。

3. **各箇所の「なぜ独立だったか」を判断したうえで取り込んだ — 充足。**
   PR 本文に13箇所それぞれの before/after と、残した3種を「サブリソースか／射影か」で切り分けた判断が残っています。とくに `gh pr diff` と `Accept: …v3.diff` の2つの綴りは同じエンドポイントの同一射影と判定して `readPullRequestDiff()` に統合、`pull-request.ts` 側にも「`gh pr diff` ではなく media type である理由」が書かれています。

4. **既存の PR 読みテストが通る（#363 のページング／再試行ポリシーのテストを含む）— 充足。**
   PR ヘッドで `bun run typecheck` clean、`bun run test` **2086 pass / 0 fail（168 files）**、`bun run lint`（`tsc --noEmit` + `synth`）clean。内訳に #363 の `list_pr_review_comments reads every page` と `merge-signals.test.ts` の再試行テスト、新規の `src/adapters/github/pull-request.test.ts`（5本: 射影が引数であること・一時障害の再試行・拒否が読みを名指すこと・JSON でない答え・オブジェクトと diff の2エンドポイント）が含まれます。#345 の直し方2・3（ページング、`merge-signals` の再試行ポリシー統一）は #363 が既に届けており、ここでは再実装せず共有リーダー経由にしただけです。

5. **契約テストを入れた場合、集合が両方向に閉じている — 充足。**
   `tests/contract/pr-read-sites.test.ts`（3本、マージ後ヘッドに存在を確認）:
   - 「only pull-request.ts reads one」— `src/**/*.ts`（テスト除く）でエンドポイントを綴るのはリーダーと `NOT_A_READ` の3ファイルだけ。
   - 「pull-request.ts spells `pr view` once」— リーダー内で argv が二重に育たないこと。
   - 「every exemption still spells the endpoint」— 免除が古くなって次の読みを隠さないこと（逆方向）。
   `NOT_A_READ` の各項目はファイル名ではなく理由文つきで列挙されています。

### クローズ条件

「親 #149 のブランチ上にマージされた PR のヘッドで上記がコードで確認できること」— 満たしています。PR #368 は `atomaton/issue-149` に MERGED、そのヘッド `8d85e67` 上で `src/adapters/github/pull-request.ts`、`src/adapters/github/pull-request.test.ts`、`tests/contract/pr-read-sites.test.ts` の実在と内容、および `merge-signals.ts` の読み込み経路を読み出して確認しました。

### 確認できなかったこと・残した判断

- **行番号でのアンカーは付けていません。** 親ブランチを手元に fetch できない（シェルの fetch が拒否される）ため、根拠は path＋関数/シンボル名（`pull-request.ts` の `viewArgs` / `readPullRequest` / `readPullRequestOrThrow` / `readPullRequestObject` / `readPullRequestDiff`、`merge-signals.ts` の `readChangedFiles`）で示しています。内容そのものは上記ヘッドから読み出した実ファイルです。
- **マージ後ヘッドでのテスト実行はありません。** `8d85e67` の check runs は deploy 系のみ（`plan-deploy` success、他 skipped）で、ユニットテストは PR ヘッドでの実行が最後です。ただしマージで書き換わったのは今回の PR のファイル群のみで、そのうち `pull-request.ts` / `pull-request.test.ts` / `pr-read-sites.test.ts` / `merge-signals.ts` はマージ後ヘッドの内容を直接読んで PR 時のものと一致することを確認しています。
- **既知の残件（ブロッカーではありません）**: レビュアーが指摘したとおり `NOT_A_READ` の免除はファイル単位なので、`mcp/github.ts` の中に「PR 自身」の `gh pr view` を新しく書き戻しても契約テストは通ってしまいます。ファイル集合が両方向に閉じていることは #364 の求めた水準どおりですが、行・呼び出し単位まで閉じたい場合は別チケット（例: 免除をファイル＋許可パターンの組にする）になります。今回はマージ済みコードに手を入れず、判断材料としてここに残します。
- 意図的に変えた挙動（戻さない前提で報告済み）: `pr-head-branch.ts` と `workspace-scope.ts` が一時的な読み失敗を再試行するようになったこと、JSON でない答え・空 stdout を「読めなかった」として扱うこと（`unreadable` 拒否、"the answer was not JSON"）。

### 次に起きること

#364 はここで完了です。残るのは親 #149 側の集約で、本サブイシューの成果（共有リーダー `src/adapters/github/pull-request.ts` と両方向に閉じた契約テスト）は `atomaton/issue-149` 上に取り込まれ済みです。冒頭で述べた `NOT_A_READ` の粒度だけは、必要なら人が別チケットとして起こす判断待ちです。"}

summary.text:
All artifacts are on the merged head of atomaton/issue-149 (8d85e67). Time to conclude.

Write the closing summary with:
- Conclusion: all four acceptance criteria met; close condition satisfied.
- Evidence per criterion with path + symbol anchors (I lack precise line numbers on the merged branch for all; I can give a few known ones). Let me be honest: anchors = path + function/symbol names. I can state file:line only where I know it. I'll use symbol anchors and say why (line numbers not readable without a branch fetch; content read from the merged branch head 8d85e67).

Actually, I could give line numbers for a couple: pull-request.ts `viewArgs` — I counted? The doc comment is long; not reliable. Skip line numbers, use symbols.

Criteria:
1. pr-by-number reads go through the shared reader; projection as argument — met: pull-request.ts with PullRequestFields/`viewArgs`, and the thirteen sites listed in the PR body now call readPullRequest / readPullRequestOrThrow / readPullRequestObject / readPullRequestDiff; verified on merged head: merge-signals.ts imports `readPullRequest` from `./pull-request.ts`.
2. Remaining independent reads explain themselves beside the code — met: merge-signals.ts `readChangedFiles` comment ("Not `pull-request.ts`'s read, and the reason is the question…"); fetch_events.ts and mcp/github.ts likewise.
3. Each site's "why independent" judged before folding in — met: per-site table in PR body (13 sites), plus the sub-resource judgement.
4. Existing PR-read tests pass — met: 2086 pass / 0 fail / 168 files on the PR head, including #363's paging (`list_pr_review_comments reads every page`) and merge-signals retry tests; new pull-request.test.ts (5) and tests/contract/pr-read-sites.test.ts (3).
5. Contract test closed both ways — met: "only pull-request.ts reads one", "pull-request.ts spells pr view once", "every exemption still spells the endpoint" (NOT_A_READ with reasons).
6. Close condition: merged into atomaton/issue-149 — met: PR #368 MERGED, issue-149 head 8d85e67 contains both files.

What I could not establish:
- The line-by-line (function-level vs line) caveat: anchors by symbol.
- Post-merge check runs on 8d85e67 are deploy-only (plan-deploy/deploy skipped/success), no unit-test run on the merged head; suite greenness is the PR-head run whose changed files are what I read on the merged branch.
- The reviewer's note: NOT_A_READ is per file, so a `pr view` of the pull request reintroduced inside mcp/github.ts would pass the contract test. Not addressed (would be a new change; criteria ask for closed set of files, which it is). Optionally file a follow-up? The reviewer called it non-blocking. Should I create a sub-issue? Issue is about to close; a follow-up issue as a child of #364 would then be orphaned/unaggregated... The tool create_sub_issue links under current issue; closing parent with open child is messy. Better: mention it in the report for #149/@yuma-seno as a known residual, leaving the decision. I think mention in the summary; not file an issue (a person can decide).
- Behaviour changes deliberately kept: retry in pr-head-branch/workspace-scope; unparsable/empty stdout = failed read.

Also mention #345's two fixes not redone (#363 delivered them).

Then call request_close_issue with reason + summary. One mention? The report is going to the issue; the machinery tells the person. I don't need to call anyone. I'll include no `/agent` and no `@login` mention — safer to mention nobody so the machinery notifies @yuma-seno. But I want to note the residual coverage gap "for @yuma-seno"? That would be a call handing work to them — actually the machinery tells them anyway. Writing "@yuma-seno" would be a call handing the work to that person, which duplicates. Better to write "the person this work belongs to" in prose? Hmm, prose referencing the role is fine but awkward. I'll just state the residual as a note without mention.

Write in Japanese? The issue/PR are in Japanese partly (#345/#149 titles Japanese) but PR body English. The repo's issue language: #364's title was Japanese-ish ("PR-by-number 読みの共有リーダーへの統合と、残す箇所の理由記述"). Tool guidance for search says use issue language. The closing comment — previous reports? I'll write in Japanese with English code anchors? Hmm. My earlier session produced a PR body in English and it was accepted. The issue is likely Japanese. I'll write the summary in Japanese since the issue title is Japanese, keeping code identifiers as-is. Mixed is fine and probably best for the owner. Actually risk: the reviewer/owner reads Japanese. Yes, go Japanese, concise.

Let me write it well-structured but not bloated.

messages.content: Issue #364 is concluded: your reason and summary are on the issue. All sub-tasks of the parent issue complete. The parent's agent was re-invoked. Nothing else is yours to do here.
